resolved.resolution: crt_sqrt owns no persistent state. Caller owns X87Context and CrtAsinRuntime; the synchronous CrtInverseFrame borrows both and owns function identity, classified double, saved CW and source-boundary metadata. X87Value is an immutable ext80 value independent of context storage; returned values remain usable with an appropriate live context. finish_crt_inverse in crt_asin.cpp is the one shared asin/acos/sqrt return/error owner. Optional matherr_control represents an unavailable source-runtime word, not actual game absence: this reference knownness enters the public CPU contract. Optional result/pending_stored_result instead describe real computation progress. Missing policy returns a computed ext80 value at the changed source CW; missing/failed handler retains its prior binary64 store and no ext80 destination. Successful bypass/handler reload restores saved CW in source order. CRT intentionally has no outer CW rollback RAII on failure; adding one would erase the current boundary contract. Lower X87 operations still restore SoftFloat TLS on arithmetic throw while retaining context sticky flags.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Actual source consumer crt_sqrt is player_mesh_math::normalize, used by normalize_mesh_vector_zero/up. It retains squared m32 spill and m64 root argument, checks failure before vector writes, performs two root m32 stores, then reciprocal/ordered component publication. MeshMathProbe and mesh unit exercise this contract; broader mesh-query/scene consumers remain maintained, even though player_mesh_math.cpp and crt_sqrt.cpp are absent from native-sources.txt at this base. crt_sqrt_extended has no maintained src call site beyond its declaration/definition in the inspected search; it remains a retained compatibility contract, not obsolete. NinjaLength -> ExactFloat::vector_length_return -> signed_square_root -> X87Context::sqrt bypasses CRT entirely; legacy signed_sqrt_extended also uses raw X87 sqrt. Its shared retained njScalor body is already integrated and must not be mistaken for a duplicate CRT/SSE root owner. CRT shares finish_crt_inverse with asin/acos, so separating unknown-policy diagnostics requires all those consumers to preserve aliases, handler reload, status and failure prefixes together. In player_mesh_query.cpp, normal normalization uses the up fallback and direction normalization uses zero fallback; each forwards the same runtime.inverse_math and propagates the nested CRT boundary before further mesh work.

semantic_review.semantic_justification: All 40 lines read: bits, body, binary64 entry and retained entry. Binary64 entry uses load_crt_binary64_argument: finite FLD64-equivalent, direct ext80 nonfinite construction preserving signaling encoding until source arithmetic. body classifies exponent/fraction/sign, saves CW, installs (saved precision bits)|0x007f for finite inputs unless saved is 0x027f, preserving precision while selecting nearest/masked setup. Quiet NaN returns through error code 7; signaling NaN adds m64 one to quiet/flag via source arithmetic and uses code 1. Negative nonzero, including negative infinity, returns ext80 indefinite/code 1; negative zero and positive infinity bypass FSQRT. Other values use X87Context::sqrt. Retained entry first spills input to binary64 for classification but computes with the original retained ext80 input; spill rounding/flags and nonfinite conversion may occur before body saves CW. This is different from scalar SSE SQRTSD and from Ninja signed-root compare/reload/sign preservation. Replacing any with std::sqrt or sharing a generic root implementation has no proof here. Source policy boundaries 0x6452ce/0x64532b are actual diagnostic PCs, unlike IEEE masks: they are passed as data in game-tier code and lack a semantic/reference mapping. Both entries lack canonical FUNCTION/LIBRARY provenance; ordinary address comments are not annotations.
